prompts.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Draw FOUR complete production animation KEY POSES for one turquoise water nest growing from level 2 to level 3. Output one transparent square source sheet in a strict 2x2 layout, read top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right. These are actual drawings to use in animation, not concept variations. Each equally sized square cell is a full 512x512 game canvas; generous transparent margins and the same fixed ground baseline at y448. The starting pool is about400px wide and the final pool about455px wide on each512px canvas. Do NOT fit or enlarge each sprite to fill its cell. No labels, text, dividers, ground shadows, background or presentation graphics.
Image1 is the exact LEVEL2 design. Image2 is the exact LEVEL3 design. Preserve their painted turquoise and mint water, dark teal outlines, soft upper-left lighting, elevated near-front view, broad low oval foreground pool and asymmetrical water curls. The viewpoint, root position and scale of individual final machinery parts are locked. Paint complete continuous contours, consistent volume and convincing occlusion.
TOP LEFT, 0.95s: the original small REAR BASIN is halfway sunk down into the original main pool. Its height and short connecting waterfall decrease together. Foreground pool still has the exact level2 width and flowing rim shape, planted at the original bottom. No machinery or stone additions yet. Nothing detaches.
TOP RIGHT, 1.40s: the same rear basin has FULLY submerged. ONE low continuous oval pool, level2 width, soft rear water rim and uninterrupted horizontal water. No raised rear bowl, no waterfall, no machinery, no empty hole. Preserve the original wavy turquoise foreground rim.
BOTTOM LEFT, 2.10s: the same low pool swells and spreads outward from its planted center to the FINAL level3 foreground width. A broad smooth connected water mantle bulges at the rear, covering the developing structure inside. This is a substantial growing water volume, not a texture change, not a rigid ring suddenly appearing. The front remains a single recognizable flowing turquoise water rim. No exposed wooden wheel, gate or tall stone tier yet.
BOTTOM RIGHT, 2.35s: the water mantle at the back begins to open and flow DOWN over the emerging upper lip of the FINAL stone rear basin. Only the upper portion of the connected final assembly is exposed. The upper wooden wheel paddles on the LEFT and the tip of the bronze-handled sluice on the RIGHT just begin to break the water at their final horizontal positions; all lower portions remain visibly submerged behind the continuous foreground pool. Never shrink the machinery; it is the FINAL size, mostly occluded by water. Water clings to and flows off the exposed surfaces. No floating loose part, mechanical part in front of the pool, spray particles, bubbles or foam.
Every drawing must show the entire nest at its prescribed growth stage with clean genuine alpha transparency. Maintain the same foreground architecture as a continuous organically changing water shape, not alternate pool designs. No artificial flashes, dissolves, duplicated rims or transparent machinery.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit image1 into ONE production key drawing of the SAME nest, just after the water mantle starts opening. Image1 is the exact edit target and framing. Image2 is the future almost-raised pose; image3 is the final architecture, only to identify the pale aqua basin material and its oval lip. Keep image1's entire foreground oval pool, front wavy rim, curled left edge, right spill lip, ground contact, width, colors and camera unchanged. Same true transparent background, one complete centered sprite, no sheet or text.
Change ONLY the REAR water mantle above the open foreground pool. The large soft turquoise bulge in image1 now slumps and parts slightly downward. At its crown, reveal ONLY one shallow pale-aqua stone oval LIP of the future upper basin, containing a narrow horizontal glimpse of water. This upper lip is still LOW: on the original512px canvas its top is at y265, waterline of the main pool is near y350, and bottom contact remains448. The whole sprite must be much lower than the finished level3 reference. The new upper lip is a slim squat oval, NOT a high tier or full tower. The lower rear structure remains completely hidden under a thick continuous opaque turquoise water sheet which flows down from the lip to the foreground pool. Absolutely NO wheel, wood, bronze handle, gate, axle, tall stone walls or mechanical fragments visible at this first emergence. The sheet of water remains connected to the pool and naturally obscures the submerged parts. Paint this specific newly exposed contour clearly, preserve the exact painterly game rendering, dark teal outlines and upper-left highlights. Do not enlarge, recenter or redesign the front pool. No holes, detached splashes, particles, foam, glow, transparency tricks or ground.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit image1 into ONE next production key pose, still PARTIALLY SUBMERGED. Image1 is the exact edit target. Image2 shows the later pose with more exposed wheel and sluice. Image3 shows the final precise machinery design. Keep image1's whole framing, foreground pool, wavy front rim, left water curl, right spill lip, width, ground contact, water palette and fixed camera exactly. True transparent background, one complete sprite, no sheet or labels.
The rear upper stone basin rises only about10px on the original512px canvas. The thick flowing turquoise mantle starts receding from its LEFT and RIGHT shoulders to expose just the UPPER THIRD of the existing final-sized machinery. On the LEFT, show only two or three upper honey-brown paddle surfaces and a short upper arc of the wooden waterwheel rim. The axle, hub and lower two thirds of the wheel remain fully covered by OPAQUE flowing turquoise water. The upper wood must be in the final wheel's position and final board thickness, not a miniature whole wheel. On the RIGHT, only the upper bronze handle and a short upper wooden edge of the attached sluice are revealed; the supports and lower gate remain underwater. These emerging partial surfaces are surrounded and overlapped by connected water that flows down their outlines into the front pool. They never float in empty space.
This is an intermediate state physically BETWEEN image1 (only pale upper basin lip exposed) and image2 (most of the wheel and gate exposed). Do not copy image2's already finished mechanical exposure. Keep a large continuous blue water curtain masking the machinery's LOWER portions so the partial emergence is unmistakable. Upper basin crest is about y240, ground448; foreground pool stays about450px wide. Upper water pours down over the submerged back assembly. No new stone tower, disconnected parts, detached water droplets, foam, splashes, sparks, glow, ghosting or semitransparent machinery. Maintain the exact rounded painted game style, thin dark teal contours, original volume and lighting.

Use case: precise-object-edit. ONE actual production key drawing, a late sinking pose of the exact water nest in image1, progressing toward the low flat pool in image2. Image1 is the edit target. Preserve the original512x512 canvas registration, entire foreground pool, width408px, wavy front silhouette, curled left edge and right spill lip EXACTLY. True transparent background, fixed viewpoint and light, no crop, no sheet or text.
Change only the small RAISED REAR BASIN. It is now almost submerged: push it DOWN and FLATTEN its tall rear wall until the upper basin becomes a very THIN LOW horizontal oval lip just barely protruding from the main pool. Its uppermost crest must be much lower than image1, around y310 instead of y289 on the512px canvas. The exposed little oval bowl is shallow and only about8-12px tall. Almost all of its vertical walls are already underwater. The original long little waterfall has shortened to a tiny connected trickle over a lip, only about4px high, merging straight into the main horizontal surface. Keep the rear oval at the same left-center horizontal location. Do not raise, enlarge or retain the original tall back bowl. This whole nest is low and flat now, clearly close to image2 but the last small back lip is still visible. Maintain one unbroken liquid body. Preserve the original hand-painted cyan/mint shading and dark teal contours. No stone, wheel, wood, handle, bubbles, foam, droplets, glow, holes or detached shapes.
